system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system under strain from overlapping shocks: regional wars and proxy attacks (Middle East, Ukraine), energy and commodity squeezes that feed inflation and political unrest, and a tech–trade rivalry that is militarizing supply chains. Fiscal stress and rising bond yields amplify policy constraints, while domestic political polarisation and shifting alliances make coordinated responses harder, producing feedbacks that intensify volatility across markets, security theatres and institutions.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and coalitions, global energy and commodity markets, international financial markets and sovereign finances, strategic supply chains (chips, AI, defence tech), major corporations and platform providers, multilateral institutions (IMF, IEA, EU, NATO), and transnational non-state actors (proxy militias, commercial shadow fleets).
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio-economic-technical-ecological system (the global human system integrating markets, technology, geopolitics, demographics and environmental constraints).
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy and commodity system (oil/diesel markets, shipping routes, strategic reserves)
International financial system (sovereign debt, bond markets, IMF/G7 policy coordination)
Global technology and trade governance (chip, AI and satellite/defence ecosystems and export controls)

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine high‑intensity war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain locked in a sustained, high‑intensity conflict marked by cross‑border strikes, cyber and intelligence operations and growing strains in Western military and intelligence support.

variables.name: Iran-led regional escalation
variables.description: Iran and its proxy networks, notably Houthi forces, are intensifying strike campaigns and hardening military and nuclear postures, raising the risk of wider confrontation with Gulf states and the United States.

variables.name: US–China tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States, China and allied partners are contesting advanced semiconductors, AI technologies and industrial markets through export controls, investment shifts and regulatory measures that are reshaping global supply chains and market access.

variables.name: Global energy and fuel supply crisis
variables.description: Global oil and refined‑fuel markets are undergoing prolonged disruption and price volatility driven by strike campaigns, logistics bottlenecks, sanctions and emergency stock releases, forcing major policy and commercial adjustments into 2027.

variables.name: Global macroeconomic and fiscal strain
variables.description: Major economies face rising inflation, higher bond yields and large fiscal deficits, prompting tighter central‑bank stances, IMF warnings and urgent fiscal consolidation that compress policy space worldwide.
